title: Aether-Continuum: Temporal Balance Invariants in a Chronos-Interpreter Self-Balancing AVL Tree
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a lightweight Chronos-Interpreter implementation of a self-balancing AVL tree that incorporates a chronologically ordered re-balancing protocol, termed Aether-Continuum. The design preserves the strict height-balance invariant while enabling deterministic key ordering under concurrent insertions. We formally verify that each rotation restores the invariant and that the tree depth remains bounded by $\lceil \log_2(n+1) \rceil$. Empirical evaluation on an Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8370C CPU @ 2.80~GHz with 1 physical core and 2 logical threads yields a mean latency of 49 241.79 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 20 308 ops/s over 30 benchmark iterations. These results confirm that the Aether-Continuum protocol incurs negligible overhead compared to classical AVL re-balancing. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Chronos-Interpreter-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261104_210244_self-balancing_avl_tree_with_a}
